title: First Identification of an Autochthonous Case of Chikungunya in Guinea.
abstract: The first confirmation of chikungunya virus infection in Guinea is reported in the present study. The patient, a 68-year-old woman presumptively diagnosed with malaria and with no history of travel, was identified through a research project focused on the etiologies of febrile illnesses in Guinea. A whole-blood sample from the patient was analyzed using multiplex reverse-transcription polymerase chain reaction, yielding a positive result for chikungunya virus, and was subsequently sequenced. The near-complete genome sequence was most closely related to strains circulating that year in Senegal. The study data are noteworthy because, despite past serological evidence of transmission, active human infection with the chikungunya virus has not previously been observed in Guinea; its emergence is linked to the identification of Aedes vectors in Dalaba. Further clinical and entomological investigations are warranted, along with country-wide genomic surveillance of arboviruses to better understand risk factors that have driven the emergence of chikungunya in Guinea and prevent possible future epidemics.
journal: American Journal of Tropical Medicine and Hygiene

title: Molecular basis for chikungunya virus recognition of a mosquito-specific receptor
abstract: Alphaviruses are arthropod-borne viruses that recognize cellular receptors in both vertebrate hosts and mosquito vectors to complete their transmission cycle, yet how they maintain recognition of receptors across evolutionarily divergent host species remains unresolved. Among alphaviruses, chikungunya virus (CHIKV), which is primarily vectored in urban settings by Aedes species mosquitoes, is the most widespread, and causes explosive outbreaks that can involve hundreds of thousands to millions of cases annually. The cell adhesion protein Lachesin is a mosquito-specific cellular receptor for CHIKV and multiple other arthritogenic alphaviruses. The envelope E2–E1 glycoproteins of these alphaviruses broadly recognize Lachesin orthologs from diverse mosquito species, but not other insects or arachnids. Lachesin genetic manipulation to prevent mosquito virus infection without interfering with endogenous receptor function could have a major impact for CHIKV control. Here, we determined high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of alphaviruses bound to Aedes albopictus Lachesin. Comparative analysis of Lachesin-bound CHIKV, Semliki Forest virus (SFV), and Middelburg virus (MIDV) revealed that these three genetically divergent viruses use a similar surface to recognize Lachesin domain 1, but with reorganized E2–E1 glycoprotein contact residues. We show that a soluble Ae. albopictus Lachesin receptor decoy protein blocks the E2–E1-mediated entry of CHIKV and other arthritogenic alphaviruses into mammalian cells with greater breadth than a vertebrate receptor MXRA8 decoy and protects against lethal SFV challenge and CHIKV pathogenesis in murine models. Additionally, we identified a naturally occurring single residue Lachesin polymorphism that is found in some Anopheles (malaria vector) mosquitoes, and fully ablates CHIKV E2–E1 recognition, informing strategies for mosquito-targeted genetic interventions that could prevent mosquito vector infection and virus transmission. These findings define distinct determinants of receptor binding in mosquitoes and humans for arthritogenic alphaviruses, with implications for countermeasure development and outbreak preparedness.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses how alphaviruses, including chikungunya virus (CHIKV), maintain receptor recognition across evolutionarily divergent host species despite their distinct cellular environments. It highlights the unresolved question of how CHIKV and related arthritogenic alphaviruses achieve broad vector specificity while interacting with mosquito-specific receptors.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The research determined high-resolution cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) structures of alphaviruses bound to the mosquito-specific receptor Lachesin from Aedes albopictus. It included comparative structural analyses of CHIKV, Semliki Forest virus (SFV), and Middelburg virus (MIDV) to elucidate receptor-binding determinants.
analysis.methods: Cryo-EM was used to resolve the structures of alphaviruses in complex with mosquito Lachesin. A soluble Aedes albopictus Lachesin receptor decoy protein was engineered and tested for its ability to block E2–E1-mediated viral entry into mammalian cells and to protect against lethal SFV challenge and CHIKV pathogenesis in murine models.
analysis.main_results: Comparative analysis revealed that CHIKV, SFV, and MIDV use a similar surface on Lachesin domain 1 for binding, but with reorganized E2–E1 glycoprotein contact residues. The Lachesin decoy protein blocked entry of CHIKV and other arthritogenic alphaviruses into mammalian cells more broadly than a vertebrate receptor MXRA8 decoy and conferred protection in murine models.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings define distinct receptor-binding determinants in mosquitoes and humans for arthritogenic alphaviruses, revealing how CHIKV maintains vector specificity while interacting with conserved mosquito receptors. This work identifies a novel mosquito-targeted strategy for blocking viral transmission through receptor decoys and genetic interventions.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The study provides a molecular basis for developing mosquito-specific countermeasures, such as receptor decoys or gene-editing strategies targeting Lachesin polymorphisms, to prevent CHIKV transmission and reduce outbreak potential. It also informs surveillance and outbreak preparedness by clarifying receptor-virus interactions critical for vector competence.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is limited to structural and functional analyses in vitro and murine models, which may not fully recapitulate human infection dynamics or mosquito vector biology. While the cryo-EM structures and decoy protein efficacy are robust, the generalizability to natural transmission settings and potential off-target effects in mosquitoes require further validation.

analysis.summary_en: This study resolves the molecular basis by which chikungunya virus (CHIKV) and related arthritogenic alphaviruses recognize the mosquito-specific receptor Lachesin across divergent vector species. Using cryo-electron microscopy, the authors determined high-resolution structures of CHIKV, Semliki Forest virus (SFV), and Middelburg virus (MIDV) bound to Aedes albopictus Lachesin, revealing that these viruses employ a conserved binding surface on Lachesin domain 1 but with distinct E2–E1 glycoprotein contact residues. A soluble Lachesin decoy protein blocked viral entry into mammalian cells more effectively than a vertebrate receptor decoy and protected mice from lethal SFV challenge and CHIKV pathogenesis. Additionally, a naturally occurring Lachesin polymorphism in Anopheles mosquitoes abolished CHIKV recognition, suggesting a target for genetic interventions to block mosquito infection. These findings define mosquito-specific receptor-binding determinants and provide a foundation for developing vector-targeted countermeasures to curb CHIKV transmission and mitigate outbreaks.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了包括 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 在内的甲病毒如何在进化上不同的 宿主 物种中维持受体识别,尽管它们的细胞环境不同。它强调了一个尚未解决的问题:CHIKV 和相关的致关节炎甲病毒如何在与蚊子特异性受体相互作用时实现广泛的 媒介 特异性。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究确定了与白纹伊蚊的蚊子特异性受体 Lachesin 结合的甲病毒的高分辨率冷冻电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构。它包括 CHIKV、塞姆利基森林病毒 (SFV) 和米德尔堡病毒 (MIDV) 的比较结构分析,以阐明受体结合决定因素。
elements_zh.methods: 冷冻电镜用于解析与蚊子 Lachesin 复合的甲病毒的结构。一种可溶性白纹伊蚊 Lachesin 受体诱饵蛋白经过工程设计并测试其阻断 E2-E1 介导的病毒进入哺乳动物细胞的能力,并在小鼠模型中防止致命的 SFV 攻击和 CHIKV 发病机制。
elements_zh.main_results: 比较分析表明,CHIKV、SFV 和 MIDV 在 Lachesin 结构域 1 上使用相似的表面进行结合,但具有重组的 E2-E1 糖蛋白接触残基。Lachesin 诱饵蛋白比脊椎动物受体 MXRA8 诱饵蛋白更广泛地阻止 CHIKV 和其他致关节炎甲病毒进入哺乳动物细胞,并在小鼠模型中提供保护。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现定义了蚊子和人类中致关节炎甲病毒的不同受体结合决定因素,揭示了 CHIKV 如何在与保守的蚊子受体相互作用时保持 媒介 特异性。这项工作确定了一种新的针对蚊子的策略,通过受体诱饵和基因干预来阻断病毒 传播。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究为开发针对蚊子的对策提供了分子基础,例如针对 Lachesin 多态性的受体诱饵或基因编辑策略,以预防 CHIKV 传播 并降低 暴发 的潜力。它还通过阐明对 媒介 能力至关重要的受体-病毒相互作用,为 监测 和 暴发 做好准备提供信息。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外和小鼠模型的结构和功能分析,这可能无法完全概括人类感染动态或蚊子 媒介 生物学。虽然冷冻电镜结构和诱饵蛋白功效很强大,但对自然 传播 设置的普遍性以及蚊子中潜在的脱靶效应需要进一步验证。

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了包括 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 在内的甲病毒如何在进化上不同的 宿主 物种中维持受体识别,尽管它们的细胞环境不同。它强调了一个尚未解决的问题:CHIKV 和相关的致关节炎甲病毒如何在与蚊子特异性受体相互作用时实现广泛的 媒介 特异性。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究确定了与白纹伊蚊的蚊子特异性受体 Lachesin 结合的甲病毒的高分辨率冷冻电子显微镜 (cryo-EM) 结构。它包括 CHIKV、塞姆利基森林病毒 (SFV) 和米德尔堡病毒 (MIDV) 的比较结构分析,以阐明受体结合决定因素。
analysis_zh.methods: 冷冻电镜用于解析与蚊子 Lachesin 复合的甲病毒的结构。一种可溶性白纹伊蚊 Lachesin 受体诱饵蛋白经过工程设计并测试其阻断 E2-E1 介导的病毒进入哺乳动物细胞的能力,并在小鼠模型中防止致命的 SFV 攻击和 CHIKV 发病机制。
analysis_zh.main_results: 比较分析表明,CHIKV、SFV 和 MIDV 在 Lachesin 结构域 1 上使用相似的表面进行结合,但具有重组的 E2-E1 糖蛋白接触残基。Lachesin 诱饵蛋白比脊椎动物受体 MXRA8 诱饵蛋白更广泛地阻止 CHIKV 和其他致关节炎甲病毒进入哺乳动物细胞,并在小鼠模型中提供保护。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 这些发现定义了蚊子和人类中致关节炎甲病毒的不同受体结合决定因素,揭示了 CHIKV 如何在与保守的蚊子受体相互作用时保持 媒介 特异性。这项工作确定了一种新的针对蚊子的策略,通过受体诱饵和基因干预来阻断病毒 传播。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该研究为开发针对蚊子的对策提供了分子基础,例如针对 Lachesin 多态性的受体诱饵或基因编辑策略,以预防 CHIKV 传播 并降低 暴发 的潜力。它还通过阐明对 媒介 能力至关重要的受体-病毒相互作用,为 监测 和 暴发 做好准备提供信息。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据仅限于体外和小鼠模型的结构和功能分析,这可能无法完全概括人类感染动态或蚊子 媒介 生物学。虽然冷冻电镜结构和诱饵蛋白功效很强大,但对自然 传播 设置的普遍性以及蚊子中潜在的脱靶效应需要进一步验证。

title: RNA Capping, Replication Complex Assembly, and Translational Regulation in Chikungunya Virus: Molecular Mechanisms and Antiviral Opportunities
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus that has become a significant global public health concern due to its rapid spread and the debilitating acute and chronic joint pain (arthralgia) it causes. Understanding the molecular events that regulate CHIKV RNA synthesis and gene expression is essential for identifying vulnerable stages in the viral life cycle and guiding the development of targeted therapies. This narrative review summarises key aspects of CHIKV molecular biology, focusing on RNA capping, genome replication, and translation. CHIKV RNA capping is primarily facilitated by non-structural protein 1 (nsP1), which has both methyltransferase and guanylyl transferase activities. These activities are necessary for producing the 5' type-0 cap structure (m7GpppN), which stabilises viral RNA, enhances translation efficiency, and aids in immune evasion. Viral genome replication takes place within membrane-derived replication spherules that compartmentalise replication complexes composed of nsP1-nsP4 and host cofactors, protecting RNA intermediates from detection by the innate immune system. The RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 drives the synthesis of negative-strand templates, followed by the amplification of positive-sense genomic RNA and the transcription of 26S sub-genomic RNA for structural protein production. CHIKV also modifies host translation and antiviral signalling to maintain efficient viral protein synthesis. These findings demonstrate that nsP1, nsP2, and nsP4 are promising antiviral targets. They emphasise the importance of understanding CHIKV's molecular mechanisms to develop effective therapeutic strategies against CHIKV and related alphaviruses.

analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: The review is a narrative synthesis summarising CHIKV molecular biology without systematic search procedures or eligibility criteria; it does not report databases, search dates, study counts, or meta-analytic methods.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: CHIKV RNA capping is mediated by non-structural protein 1 (nsP1) with methyltransferase and guanylyl transferase activities to produce a 5' type-0 cap (m7GpppN), which stabilises viral RNA, enhances translation, and aids immune evasion; replication occurs in membrane-derived spherules containing nsP1–nsP4 and host cofactors, protecting intermediates from innate immunity; nsP4 functions as the RNA-dependent RNA polymerase, synthesising negative-strand templates and amplifying positive-sense genomic RNA and 26S sub-genomic RNA for structural proteins.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not address heterogeneity across CHIKV lineages or conflicting findings regarding host cofactor dependencies in replication complex assembly; it lacks quantitative data on translation modulation mechanisms and does not evaluate the robustness of nsP1–nsP4 interactions across experimental systems.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: Prioritise structural and functional characterisation of nsP1-mediated capping and nsP4 polymerase activity to enable structure-guided antiviral design; investigate host cofactors in replication spherules to identify host-directed therapeutic targets; develop assays to quantify CHIKV translation modulation and immune evasion mechanisms for translational control interventions.

Replication occurs in membrane-derived spherules containing nsP1–nsP4 and host cofactors, shielding RNA intermediates from innate immunity. The RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 drives negative-strand synthesis, positive-sense RNA amplification, and 26S sub-genomic RNA transcription for structural proteins. These processes highlight nsP1, nsP2, and nsP4 as antiviral targets. Key gaps include limited quantitative data on translation modulation, unaddressed lineage-specific heterogeneity, and insufficient evaluation of host cofactor dependencies.

They emphasise the importance of understanding CHIKV's molecular mechanisms to develop effective therapeutic strategies against CHIKV and related alphaviruses.

analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 该综述是对 CHIKV 分子生物学的叙述性综合总结,没有系统的检索程序或资格标准;它不报告数据库、搜索日期、研究计数或荟萃分析方法。

media_mentions.content_title: RNA Capping, Replication Complex Assembly, and Translational Regulation in Chikungunya Virus: Molecular Mechanisms and Antiviral Opportunities
media_mentions.content: Abstract Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging mosquito-borne alphavirus that has become a significant global public health concern due to its rapid spread and the debilitating acute and chronic joint pain (arthralgia) it causes. Understanding the molecular events that regulate CHIKV RNA synthesis and gene expression is essential for identifying vulnerable stages in the viral life cycle and guiding the development of targeted therapies. This narrative review summarises key aspects of CHIKV molecular biology, focusing on RNA capping, genome replication, and translation. CHIKV RNA capping is primarily facilitated by non-structural protein 1 (nsP1), which has both methyltransferase and guanylyl transferase activities. These activities are necessary for producing the 5' type-0 cap structure (m7GpppN), which stabilises viral RNA, enhances translation efficiency, and aids in immune evasion. Viral genome replication takes place within membrane-derived replication spherules that compartmentalise replication complexes composed of nsP1-nsP4 and host cofactors, protecting RNA intermediates from detection by the innate immune system. The RNA-dependent RNA polymerase nsP4 drives the synthesis of negative-strand templates, followed by the amplification of positive-sense genomic RNA and the transcription of 26S sub-genomic RNA for structural protein production. CHIKV also modifies host translation and antiviral signalling to maintain efficient viral protein synthesis. These findings demonstrate that nsP1, nsP2, and nsP4 are promising antiviral targets. They emphasise the importance of understanding CHIKV's molecular mechanisms to develop effective therapeutic strategies against CHIKV and related alphaviruses. Introduction & Background Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an arthropod-borne virus (arbovirus) that belongs to the genus Alphavirus within the family Togaviridae. First isolated during an outbreak in Tanzania in 1952, CHIKV has become a significant global public health concern due to its rapid geographical spread and its capacity to cause large-scale epidemics. The virus is primarily transmitted through the bites of infected mosquitoes, specifically Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus, which are widespread in tropical and subtropical regions [1]. Over the past two decades, recurrent outbreaks in Africa, Asia, Europe, and the Americas have underscored the epidemic potential of CHIKV and highlighted the urgent need for effective antiviral therapies and preventive strategies [1,2]. CHIKV infection is characterised by an acute febrile illness accompanied by severe polyarthralgia, myalgia, headache, fatigue, and skin rash. Although mortality rates remain relatively low, persistent joint pain and musculoskeletal complications may continue for months or even years after the acute phase of infection, significantly affecting the quality of life of affected individuals [3]. The socioeconomic burden associated with chronic chikungunya disease has become increasingly evident, particularly in endemic regions where healthcare resources are limited. Despite its growing global impact, no specific antiviral treatment has yet been approved for CHIKV infection, making a detailed understanding of its molecular biology essential for the development of targeted therapeutic interventions [4]. CHIKV possesses a positive-sense single-stranded RNA genome approximately 11.8 kb in length. The viral genome contains a 5′ methylated cap structure and a 3′ polyadenylated tail, allowing it to function directly as messenger RNA upon entry into the host cell [3]. Two major open reading frames encode the viral non-structural and structural proteins. The non-structural proteins (nsP1-nsP4) are responsible for RNA synthesis, genome replication, RNA capping, and modulation of host cellular pathways, whereas the structural proteins mediate viral assembly, entry, and release. Successful viral replication depends on the coordinated interaction of these proteins with host cellular factors and intracellular membranes [5]. Among the various stages of the CHIKV replication cycle, RNA capping, replication complex (RC) assembly, and translational regulation represent critical molecular events that determine viral fitness and pathogenicity. RNA capping, primarily mediated by the multifunctional enzyme nsP1, generates a type-0 cap structure at the 5′ end of viral RNAs [2]. This modification enhances RNA stability, promotes efficient translation, and enables the virus to evade host innate immune recognition. Simultaneously, viral replication occurs within specialised membrane-bound replication organelles known as spherules, where replication complexes composed of nsP1-nsP4 orchestrate the synthesis of genomic and sub-genomic RNAs [4]. Furthermore, CHIKV manipulates host translational machinery and antiviral signalling pathways to ensure preferential translation of viral proteins while suppressing host gene expression. Recent advances in structural biology, cryo-electron microscopy, and molecular virology have significantly improved our understanding of these interconnected processes. These discoveries have revealed several highly conserved viral enzymes and replication components as attractive antiviral targets [5]. This narrative review seeks to combine current knowledge about RNA capping, the assembly of the RC, and translational regulation. These interconnected molecular processes collectively control the replication of CHIKV, its ability to evade the immune system, and the synthesis of viral proteins. By understanding how these mechanisms interact, we can identify novel antiviral targets and guide the development of future therapeutic interventions against CHIKV. Figure 1 shows the genome organisation and expression of Chikungunya. Review Search strategy A narrative review was conducted to summarise current evidence on CHIKV RNA capping, RC assembly, and translational regulation. A narrative literature search was performed using PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar. The primary search period included studies published from January 2000 to March 2025, while older landmark publications were included to provide historical context on alphavirus molecular biology. The search strategy combined Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) terms and free-text keywords, including “Chikungunya virus,” “CHIKV,” “alphavirus,” “RNA capping,” “nsP1,” “methyltransferase,” “guanylyltransferase,” “replication complex,” “replication organelle,” “replication spherules,” “nsP2 protease,” “nsP3,” “stress granules,” “nsP4 polymerase,” “subgenomic RNA,” “26S RNA,” “translation,” “host shutoff,” and “innate immune response.” Boolean operators (AND/OR) were applied to refine database searches. Additional relevant studies were identified through manual screening of reference lists and citation tracking. Records were screened by title and abstract, and eligible full texts were assessed for relevance. Eligible studies included mechanistic studies, structural biology studies, in vitro studies, animal studies, antiviral screening studies, and relevant review articles that investigated CHIKV molecular biology, RNA capping, RC assembly, translational regulation, or antiviral development. Non-English articles, conference abstracts, unpublished reports, editorials without evidence, and purely clinical case reports were excluded. Duplicates were removed before full-text review. Data were extracted manually and synthesised narratively, and findings were organised thematically. RNA capping and its biological significance in CHIKV RNA capping is an essential post-transcriptional modification at the 5′ end of eukaryotic and some viral RNAs, involving the addition of a methylated guanosine through a 5′-5′ triphosphate linkage. This cap enhances RNA stability, facilitates translation, and helps viral RNAs avoid host immune detection. In positive-sense RNA viruses like CHIKV, capping is important as the viral genome directly functions as mRNA, efficiently recruiting host ribosomes for protein synthesis [6]. The canonical cap 0 structure (m7GpppN) is formed via enzymatic reactions: removal of the γ-phosphate by RNA triphosphatase, GMP transfer by guanylyl transferase, and methylation at the N7 position by methyltransferase. In some organisms, an additional 2′-O methylation creates a cap 1 structure (m7GpppNm), enhancing translation and evading innate immune sensors like RIG-I and MDA5 [7]. In CHIKV, the 5′ cap is a determinant of viral fitness. It promotes cap-dependent translation initiation by enabling recognition by the host eIF4E initiation factor, ensuring synthesis of viral non-structural and structural proteins [7]. The cap also protects viral RNA from degradation by host exonucleases, preserving genome integrity in the cytoplasm [8]. Mutations affecting the viral capping enzyme nsP1 impair cap formation, reduce translation efficiency, increase interferon induction, and attenuate viral replication [9,10]. Viral capping machinery and cap synthesis mechanism: nsP1 as the central enzyme CHIKV RNA capping is primarily mediated by nsP1, which acts as the main enzyme responsible for generating the 5′ type-0 cap structure (m7GpppN) on both genomic and sub-genomic RNAs [7,8,11]. Unlike host mRNA capping, which involves multiple enzymes acting sequentially, CHIKV relies on nsP1 as a multifunctional capping factor that possesses both methyltransferase and guanylyltransferase activities [7,11]. In addition to its enzymatic roles, nsP1 associates with the plasma membrane and endosomal membranes, contributing to the formation of membrane-anchored replication spherules that provide a specialised environment for RNA synthesis and processing. Alphavirus capping employs a unique “methylation-first” strategy in which nsP1 methylates GTP with S-adenosyl-L-methionine (SAM), producing 7-methylguanosine triphosphate (m7GTP) and S-adenosyl-L-homocysteine (SAH). The methylated nucleotide is then linked to a conserved histidine residue (His37) in the nsP1 active site, creating a transient m7GMP-enzyme intermediate [8,11]. Subsequently, nsP1 transfers the m7GMP moiety to the 5′ diphosphate end of the nascent viral RNA, generating the mature m7GpppN cap structure. This reversed order of reactions-methylation before guanylylation distinguishes alphaviruses from the canonical host capping pathway [12]. Figure 2 shows the CHIKV RNA capping mechanism mediated by nsP1 [13]. Membrane association The membrane association of nsP1 is vital for organising CHIKV replication and capping machinery in specialised intracellular compartments. It anchors the RC to modified host membranes, such as those of the plasma membrane and endosomes, facilitating the formation of replication spherules [14,15]. These structures create a protected niche for viral RNA synthesis, shielding the viral genome from host defences [15]. The attachment of nsP1 to membranes is aided by an amphipathic α-helix at its C-terminus, which interacts with the lipid bilayer. Palmitoylation at conserved cysteine residues enhances nsP1's hydrophobic interactions, regulating its localisation and activity. If palmitoylation is lost or the helix is disrupted, it impairs membrane binding and reduces the efficiency of viral replication [14]. Membrane-bound nsP1 forms dodecameric oligomers that recruit other non-structural proteins and host factors necessary for RNA replication, ensuring efficient viral replication by coupling enzymatic function with spatial organisation [15]. Mechanism of cap synthesis CHIKV RNA capping involves three reactions: (a) removal of the γ-phosphate by nsP2’s triphosphatase activity, (b) guanylylation mediated by nsP1 to form a 5′-5′ link, and (c) N7-methylation by nsP1 using SAM as a methyl donor [7,15]. This process converts the 5′ triphosphate end of viral RNA into a methylated cap structure (m7GpppN-RNA), important for RNA stability, translation, and immune evasion. It starts with nsP2 removing the γ-phosphate, creating a diphosphate intermediate (ppN-RNA). nsP1 then methylates GTP to form m7GTP and links it to produce an m7GMP-enzyme intermediate. nsP1 transfers the methylated guanine to the diphosphate RNA, yielding the m7GpppN cap [15]. This capping pathway allows for effective ribosome recruitment and helps evade immune detection by sensors like RIG-I and MDA5 [7]. Cap structure The 5′ cap structure of CHIKV RNA acts as a molecular signature throughout the viral life cycle, facilitating efficient gene expression, RNA stability, and evasion of host immune defences. This methylated cap (m7GpppN-RNA) mimics host mRNAs, allowing CHIKV to utilise the host's translational machinery while avoiding activation of antiviral pathways [7]. The cap on viral RNA aids translation initiation by being recognised by eIF4E, which helps form the initiation complex. Without proper capping, viral RNAs have difficulty engaging with the host's translation machinery, leading to reduced protein production and viral replication. The cap protects CHIKV RNA from exonuclease degradation, preserving its integrity [15]. The N7-methylated guanine cap is important for immune evasion, as it hides viral RNA from cytoplasmic sensors, reducing interferon-mediated antiviral responses. Proper capping is essential for viral replication and pathogenicity; mutations in this process lower RNA stability and viral growth [11]. RC assembly and polyprotein cleavage switching in CHIKV Replication of the CHIKV genome occurs within a highly organised membrane-associated RC, which serves as the central platform for viral RNA synthesis, sub-genomic transcription, and RNA processing [16,17]. This RC is primarily composed of the four viral non-structural proteins (nsP1-nsP4), together with host factors and remodelled intracellular membranes that provide a protected microenvironment for replication. Following viral entry and uncoating, the RNA genome functions directly as mRNA and is translated into polyprotein precursors (P123 and P1234) [18,19]. These polyproteins are subsequently processed by the viral nsP2 protease into mature nsP proteins, thereby enabling maturation of the functional RC. RC assembly occurs in invaginated membrane structures called spherules, derived mainly from the plasma membrane and endosomal compartments, which shield viral RNA replication intermediates from host innate immune sensors and enhance replication efficiency [17,19]. Each of the four CHIKV non-structural proteins (nsP1-nsP4) performs distinct but interconnected functions during viral replication. nsP1 mediates RNA capping and membrane anchoring, nsP2 possesses protease and helicase activities, nsP3 functions as a scaffold for host protein interactions, and nsP4 serves as the viral RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). nsP1 acts as the membrane anchor and viral capping enzyme, promoting spherule formation through palmitoylation-dependent membrane association [12]. nsP2 possesses helicase and protease activities, enabling RNA unwinding and controlling polyprotein cleavage. nsP3 functions as a scaffolding protein that stabilises RC assembly and recruits host proteins such as G3BP to support replication. nsP4 serves as the RdRp and catalyses synthesis of both negative- and positive-sense viral RNA strands [19]. A regulatory checkpoint in CHIKV replication is the ordered cleavage of the non-structural polyproteins, which acts as a molecular switch controlling the transition from negative-strand to positive-strand RNA synthesis [18]. Early in infection, the RC predominantly contains uncleaved P123 associated with nsP4, forming an immature complex specialised for the synthesis of the complementary negative-strand RNA template [20]. As infection progresses, sequential cleavage of P123 by nsP2 generates mature nsP1-nsP4, producing a fully active RC that preferentially drives synthesis of positive-sense genomic RNA and transcription of the 26S subgenomic RNA required for structural protein expression [18]. The genome of CHIKV encodes four non-structural proteins (nsP1-nsP4) that play an important role in viral replication, as well as five structural proteins (Capsid, E3, E2, 6K/TF, and E1) that are responsible for virion assembly, maturation, and entry into host cells. A summary of the major functions of these proteins is provided in Table 1. RC localisation and RNA synthesis in CHIKV Replication of CHIKV occurs within specialised membrane-bound RCs that form mainly on the plasma membrane and endosomal membranes [16]. These RCs concentrate viral non-structural proteins (nsP1-nsP4), host cofactors, and RNA intermediates, creating protected microenvironments that enhance replication efficiency while shielding viral RNA from host antiviral sensors, such as RIG-I and MDA5 [25]. Spherule formation is initiated early in infection when nsP1 anchors the replication machinery to membranes through palmitoylation and electrostatic interactions, inducing membrane invagination to generate spherules (~50-70 nm) [16]. These vesicular structures function as replication factories, providing high local concentrations of enzymes and protecting replicating RNA from cytoplasmic nucleases [17]. During negative-strand synthesis, the early RC (P123-nsP4) produces a complementary negative-sense RNA template, which is essential for downstream RNA amplification. As infection progresses and polyprotein cleavage generates mature nsP proteins, the RC switches to positive-strand synthesis, producing new genomic RNA for packaging and translation [18]. Simultaneously, transcription of the 26S sub-genomic RNA is initiated from an internal promoter on the negative strand, ensuring high-level expression of structural proteins required for virion assembly [17]. The dynamic trafficking of RCs further regulates replication. Initially, replication occurs at the plasma membrane, but later RCs are internalised and accumulate in endosomal and lysosomal compartments, supporting coordination between RNA synthesis…

title: Luciferase unleashed: Lighting the path to vaccine approval using a novel high-throughput chikungunya virus neutralization assay
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) neutralization assays, which measure virus-neutralizing activity, play a pivotal role in evaluating vaccine effectiveness and monitoring immunity. As CHIKV continues to spread beyond endemic tropical regions, causing more frequent outbreaks and debilitating disease, it remains a serious global health concern. Vaccination can help alleviate these burdens by inducing neutralizing antibodies, which are also produced following natural infection. Neutralizing antibodies can prevent virus infection and are considered a key correlate of protection against disease caused by CHIKV. Accurate assessment of neutralizing antibodies is therefore essential for both vaccine evaluation and public health surveillance. This work introduces a validated luciferase-based high-throughput CHIKV neutralization assay (CHIKV-luc NT 80 ) for quantifying serum neutralizing antibodies. The assay uses a genetically engineered reporter virus (CHIKV181/25-luc) that expresses luciferase, allowing in vitro viral infectivity to be measured using luminescence rather than manual plaque counting. Compared to the traditional plaque reduction neutralization test (PRNT), this method is faster, easier, more reproducible, and better suited for large-scale clinical studies associated with a high biological sample burden, due to its scalability. The use of a stringent 80% neutralization titer threshold (NT 80 ) also provides a more stringent measure of antibodies compared to conventional NT 50 values. The assay was compared to other methods, having high concordance (r ≈ 0.9) and low bias (≤15%), supporting its analytical reliability, qualified for phase 2 clinical trials, and validated for phase 3 clinical sample testing. The assay contributed to the establishment of the first World Health Organization International Standard for anti-CHIKV (code number 1502/19), and its results harmonized well with other virus neutralization methods. Neutralization titer results from preclinical and clinical serum sample testing supported the characterization of a surrogate threshold of protection, and licensure of VIMKUNYA (CHIKV virus-like particle [VLP] vaccine).

abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 中和测定可测量病毒中和活​​性,在评估 疫苗 有效性和监测免疫力方面发挥着关键作用。随着 CHIKV 继续在流行的热带地区传播,导致更频繁的 暴发 和使人衰弱的疾病,它仍然是一个严重的全球健康问题。疫苗接种 可以通过诱导中和抗体来帮助减轻这些负担,中和抗体也在自然感染后产生。中和抗体可以预防病毒感染,被认为是预防 CHIKV 引起的疾病的关键相关因素。因此,准确评估中和抗体对于 疫苗 评估和公共卫生 监测 至关重要。这项工作介绍了一种经过验证的基于荧光素酶的高通量 CHIKV 中和测定 (CHIKV-luc NT 80 ),用于定量血清中和抗体。该检测使用表达荧光素酶的基因工程报告病毒(CHIKV181/25-luc),允许使用发光而不是手动噬菌斑计数来测量体外病毒感染性。与传统的斑块减少中和试验(PRNT)相比,该方法更快、更容易、重现性更好,并且由于其可扩展性,更适合与高生物样本负荷相关的大规模临床研究。与传统的 NT 50 值相比,严格的 80% 中和效价阈值 (NT 80 ) 的使用还提供了更严格的抗体测量。该检测与其他方法相比,具有高一致性(r ≈ 0.9)和低偏倚(≤15%),支持其分析可靠性,符合 2 期临床试验资格,并经过 3 期临床样本测试验证。该测定有助于建立第一个世界卫生组织抗 CHIKV 国际标准(代码号 1502/19),其结果与其他病毒中和方法很好地协调一致。临床前和临床血清样本测试的中和滴度结果支持替代阈值的表征以及 VIMKUNYA(CHIKV 病毒样颗粒 [VLP] 疫苗)的许可。

title: Chikungunya Virus Mosquito Vectors: A Global Review of Field Surveillance and Laboratory Vector Competence (2020–2026)
abstract: The chikungunya virus (CHIKV) is an emerging alphavirus transmitted primarily by Aedes mosquitoes. This narrative review synthesised evidence from 56 mosquito-based records (34 field surveillance records and 22 laboratory vector competence records) published from January 2020 to June 2026. Aedes aegypti was the most frequently detected species, confirmed as CHIKV-positive in 22 of the 29 field studies that examined it, followed by Aedes albopictus (positive in nine of 12). Both species demonstrated consistent laboratory competence. Descriptive laboratory analysis showed mean infection, dissemination, and transmission values of approximately 76%, 77%, and 37% for Ae. aegypti, and 79%, 80%, and 47% for Ae. albopictus, respectively; these values are descriptive summaries across heterogeneous laboratory protocols and inconsistently reported genotypes. East/Central/South African–Indian Ocean Lineage of the chikungunya virus (ECSA-IOL) showed the highest mean transmission efficiency among genotype groups. In addition, CHIKV RNA was also detected in Culex quinquefasciatus, Psorophora spp., Wyeomyia spp., and other culicids in field studies, but laboratory evidence does not support these species as confirmed competent vectors. Other Aedes species, including Aedes vittatus, Aedes polynesiensis, Aedes koreicus, and Aedes japonicus, may have regional relevance but require further validation. Key evidence gaps include incomplete genotype reporting, limited virus isolation from positive mosquito pools, and inconsistent transmission metrics. Future preparedness for CHIKV emergence and spread requires integrated surveillance combining field detection, virus isolation, genomic sequencing, and standardised vector competence assays within an integrated surveillance framework.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review focuses on chikungunya virus (CHIKV) mosquito vectors, examining field surveillance and laboratory vector competence evidence from 2020–2026. The central question concerns the global distribution and competence of mosquito species in transmitting CHIKV.

title: Chikungunya vaccine approval in Brazil: navigating through epidemiological challenges and immunisation strategies
abstract: Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) can cause acute arboviral illness, usually accompanied by severe polyarthralgia. In 2025, live-attenuated CHIKV vaccine Ixchiq® (Valneva, Saint-Herblain, France) was authorised for use in Brazil, where CHIKV often co-circulates with other arboviruses. A central public health question emerges: how should this vaccine be optimally deployed in a country characterised by hyperendemic transmission, frequent underdiagnosis, and marked regional disparities? We conducted an epidemiological analysis using notified CHIKV cases from the Notifiable Diseases Information System (SINAN) and socioeconomic indicators from the Brazilian Human Development Atlas. This framework enabled the identification of municipal clusters with shared epidemiological and socioeconomic profiles, allowing exploration of the relationship between disease notification rate and social health determinants. Our results showed that CHIKV transmission exhibited a cyclic pattern with geographic expansion toward the Southeast/South — Brazil’s most densely populated regions characterised by low population immunity. Cluster analyses showed that the greatest disease burden is concentrated in socioeconomically disadvantaged municipalities, particularly in the Northeast, where healthcare disparities may further impact diagnostic capacity. abstract_zh: 基孔肯雅病毒 (CHIKV) 可引起急性虫媒病毒性疾病,通常伴有严重的多关节痛。2025 年,减毒活 CHIKV 疫苗 Ixchiq®(Valneva,Saint-Herblain,法国)被授权在巴西使用,因为 CHIKV 经常与其他虫媒病毒在巴西共同传播。出现了一个核心公共卫生问题:在一个以 传播 高流行、经常漏诊和明显地区差异为特征的国家,应该如何最佳部署 疫苗?我们利用法定疾病信息系统 (SINAN) 通报的 CHIKV 病例和巴西人类发展地图集的社会经济指标进行了流行病学分析。该框架能够识别具有共同流行病学和社会经济概况的城市群,从而可以探索疾病通知率与社会健康决定因素之间的关系。我们的结果表明,CHIKV 传播 表现出一种循环模式,其地理范围向东南/南部扩展——巴西人口最稠密的地区,其特点是人群免疫力低。聚类分析表明,最大的疾病负担集中在社会经济条件较差的城市,特别是在东北部,那里的医疗保健差异可能会进一步影响诊断能力。根据所获得的结果,我们认为应采取混合免疫策略,从东北部高 发病率 城市开始,到达东南部主要城市中心,以预防更大的 暴发。实施还必须考虑到当前高危人群中的 疫苗 禁忌症,并以实时流行病学和昆虫学 监测 为指导。

title: Hybrid SINDy-EnKF in Learning Chikungunya Dynamics from Incomplete, Noisy or Partially Observed Data
abstract: Current mechanistic models for the transmission dynamics of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) rely on uncertain parameters or partially observed data. This limitation challenges the use of theoretical models for understanding and forecasting disease spread. Here we present a hybrid, data-driven model framework that combines Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) with the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) for sequential data assimilation. Our numerical experiments show that this approach improves prediction accuracy and provides a good reconstruction of unobserved trajectories under partial observability, a common constraint in real-world epidemiological surveillance. SINDy can be applied to epidemic trajectories, recovering the underlying equations in noise-free conditions. However, standalone SINDy is highly sensitive to noise, leading to spurious terms and poor performance. Hence, we embed the identification procedure within an EnKF framework, which assimilates noisy observations to correct forecast states from the SINDy-derived model and to infer unobserved state variables.

source_body_en: Current mechanistic models for the transmission dynamics of the Chikungunya virus (CHIKV) rely on uncertain parameters or partially observed data. This limitation challenges the use of theoretical models for understanding and forecasting disease spread. Here we present a hybrid, data-driven model framework that combines Sparse Identification of Nonlinear Dynamics (SINDy) with the Ensemble Kalman Filter (EnKF) for sequential data assimilation. Our numerical experiments show that this approach improves prediction accuracy and provides a good reconstruction of unobserved trajectories under partial observability, a common constraint in real-world epidemiological surveillance. SINDy can be applied to epidemic trajectories, recovering the underlying equations in noise-free conditions. However, standalone SINDy is highly sensitive to noise, leading to spurious terms and poor performance. Hence, we embed the identification procedure within an EnKF framework, which assimilates noisy observations to correct forecast states from the SINDy-derived model and to infer unobserved state variables.

analysis_zh.methods: 该方法将 SINDy 识别过程嵌入 EnKF 框架中,以吸收噪声观测值、根据 SINDy 派生模型纠正预测状态,并推断未观测到的状态变量。
analysis_zh.main_results: 数值实验表明,这种混合方法提高了预测精度,并在部分可观察性下提供了未观察到的轨迹的良好重建,这是现实世界流行病学 监测 中的常见约束。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 虽然 SINDy 可以在无噪声条件下恢复基础方程,但独立的 SINDy 对噪声高度敏感,导致杂散项和性能不佳;混合 SINDy-EnKF 框架通过集成数据同化解决了这一限制。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 该方法增强了CHIKV动力学建模的可靠性,支持更好的监测、基孔肯雅热和感染的预测和干预策略。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 证据基于数值实验,虽然该方法显示出希望,但其在不同流行病学条件下的实际适用性和性能需要进一步验证。

title: Virus-specific alterations in placental structure and transporter expression following maternal arbovirus infection.
abstract: We hypothesized that arboviruses impair the placental expression of key functional markers implicated in fetal brain development. Singleton placentae (n = 54) affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed. Immunohistochemical quantification of key transporter systems, cell turnover markers, and signalling pathways related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was undertaken. Maternal age and BMI were lower in CHIKV/ZIKV, whereas birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC. CHIKV/ZIKV exhibited reduced syncytiotrophoblast area, CHIKV/DENV showed reduced syncytial knot area, whereas DENV showed increased fetal blood vessel and reduced connective tissue areas. Histopathology detected predominantly mild vascular and stromal lesions across groups, with DENV placentae exhibiting moderate congestion in 100% of cases. Decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 were detected in all groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also exhibited decreased GLUT1, while ZIKV showed reduced SNAT1 expression. MCT8 expression was significantly elevated in CHIKV. Placental Ki-67 was increased in CHIKV/ZIKV, indicating altered trophoblast turnover. VEGFB expression was reduced and p-mTOR signalling was increased across all arbovirus-exposed placentae, while MMP9 expression was unchanged. Principal components analysis (PCA) distinguished infected from uninfected groups based on placental functional markers related to fetal brain development, but not on histomorphometry. Arboviral-infected placentae showed distinct structural remodelling and altered transporter expression, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability and long-term neurodevelopmental risks, even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. KEY POINTS: Virus-specific placental histomorphometric changes were detected, including altered syncytiotrophoblast/syncytial knot, connective tissue and fetal blood vessel areas. Arboviruses reduced the placental efflux transporters P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) and disrupted the expression of ABCA1, SNAT2, GLUT1 and SNAT4 nutrient transporters, while ZIKV additionally reduced SNAT1 expression. Placental functional adaptation to arboviral infection comprised changes in the expression of placental markers of proliferation (Ki-67), angiogenesis (VEGFB), and nutrient sensing (p-mTOR). Arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibited greater functional alterations rather than overt structural pathology, suggesting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment, even in the absence of major neonatal abnormalities.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to investigate whether arboviruses impair placental expression of key functional markers involved in fetal brain development, addressing a gap in understanding how maternal infections might affect placental function and fetal outcomes.
analysis.study_design_and_population: Singleton placentae (n = 54) affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed to compare structural and functional changes across groups.
analysis.methods: Immunohistochemical quantification of key transporter systems, cell turnover markers, and signalling pathways related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was undertaken to assess placental alterations.
analysis.main_results: Maternal age and BMI were lower in CHIKV/ZIKV, whereas birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC. CHIKV/ZIKV exhibited reduced syncytiotrophoblast area, CHIKV/DENV showed reduced syncytial knot area, whereas DENV showed increased fetal blood vessel and reduced connective tissue areas. Decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 were detected in all groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also exhibited decreased GLUT1, while ZIKV showed reduced SNAT1 expression. analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The findings suggest that virus-specific placental histomorphometric changes were detected, including altered syncytiotrophoblast/syncytial knot, connective tissue and fetal blood vessel areas, highlighting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: The results may inform surveillance and diagnostic strategies for placental changes associated with arbovirus infections, particularly in identifying risks for fetal brain development and long-term neurodevelopmental outcomes.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study detected functional alterations rather than overt structural pathology, which may limit the ability to draw definitive conclusions about causal relationships, but the evidence is moderate in strength due to the use of immunohistochemical quantification and comparative analysis.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the effects of maternal arbovirus infection on placental structure and transporter expression, focusing on chikungunya virus (CHIKV). Singleton placentae from CHIKV, dengue (DENV), zika (ZIKV), and healthy controls were examined. Immunohistochemical analysis revealed reduced syncytiotrophoblast and syncytial knot areas in CHIKV/DENV, increased fetal blood vessel areas in DENV, and decreased expression of key transporters like P-gp, BCRP, and SNAT2 across all infected groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also showed increased Ki-67 expression, indicating altered trophoblast turnover. VEGFB expression was reduced, and p-mTOR signalling was increased in all arbovirus-exposed placentae. These findings suggest potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment, even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. title_zh: 母体虫媒病毒感染后胎盘结构和转运蛋白表达的病毒特异性改变。
source_body_en: We hypothesized that arboviruses impair the placental expression of key functional markers implicated in fetal brain development. Singleton placentae (n = 54) affected by chikungunya (CHIKV, n = 12), dengue (DENV, n = 8), zika (ZIKV, n = 15), or healthy controls (HC, n = 15) were analysed. Immunohistochemical quantification of key transporter systems, cell turnover markers, and signalling pathways related to extracellular matrix remodelling, vascular maintenance, and nutrient sensing was undertaken. Maternal age and BMI were lower in CHIKV/ZIKV, whereas birth weight was reduced in DENV pregnancies compared with HC. CHIKV/ZIKV exhibited reduced syncytiotrophoblast area, CHIKV/DENV showed reduced syncytial knot area, whereas DENV showed increased fetal blood vessel and reduced connective tissue areas. Histopathology detected predominantly mild vascular and stromal lesions across groups, with DENV placentae exhibiting moderate congestion in 100% of cases. Decreased expression of P-gp, BCRP, ABCA1 and SNAT2 were detected in all groups. CHIKV/ZIKV also exhibited decreased GLUT1, while ZIKV showed reduced SNAT1 expression. MCT8 expression was significantly elevated in CHIKV. Placental Ki-67 was increased in CHIKV/ZIKV, indicating altered trophoblast turnover. VEGFB expression was reduced and p-mTOR signalling was increased across all arbovirus-exposed placentae, while MMP9 expression was unchanged. Principal components analysis (PCA) distinguished infected from uninfected groups based on placental functional markers related to fetal brain development, but not on histomorphometry. Arboviral-infected placentae showed distinct structural remodelling and altered transporter expression, potentially increasing fetal brain vulnerability and long-term neurodevelopmental risks, even in the absence of neonatal symptoms. KEY POINTS: Virus-specific placental histomorphometric changes were detected, including altered syncytiotrophoblast/syncytial knot, connective tissue and fetal blood vessel areas. Arboviruses reduced the placental efflux transporters P-glycoprotein (P-gp) and breast cancer resistance protein (BCRP) and disrupted the expression of ABCA1, SNAT2, GLUT1 and SNAT4 nutrient transporters, while ZIKV additionally reduced SNAT1 expression. Placental functional adaptation to arboviral infection comprised changes in the expression of placental markers of proliferation (Ki-67), angiogenesis (VEGFB), and nutrient sensing (p-mTOR). Arbovirus-exposed placentae exhibited greater functional alterations rather than overt structural pathology, suggesting potential subclinical effects on fetal neurodevelopment, even in the absence of major neonatal abnormalities.

title: Evaluation of Larvicidal Potential of Nepeta cataria and Cymbopogon nardus Essential Oils Against Aedes aegypti.
abstract: Mosquito-borne diseases remain one of the greatest challenges to global public health, with Aedes aegypti (A. aegypti) serving as a primary vector of arboviruses such as dengue, chikungunya, yellow fever, and Zika. Reliance on synthetic insecticides for larval control has contributed to ecological concerns, human health risks, and the emergence of resistance in mosquito populations. These issues highlight the urgent need for safer, sustainable, and environmentally compatible alternatives. The present study investigated the larvicidal efficacy of essential oils extracted from locally grown plants. Cymbopogon nardus (C. nardus) (citronella) and Nepeta cataria (N. cataria) (catnip) as potential botanical substitutes in the scenario of changing climate. Fresh plant materials were authenticated, processed, and subjected to solvent extraction. The chemical composition of both oils was characterized using gas chromatography-mass spectrometry (GC-MS), which confirmed several phytoconstituents of biological importance, including citronellol, citronellal, geraniol, and nepetalactone isomers. Larvicidal bioassays were performed against A. aegypti using two stock concentrations (1 and 0.1%) at variable doses, with mortality monitored after 24, 48, and 72 h of exposure. Both essential oils demonstrated evident dose- and time-dependent mortality, with complete larval death observed at higher concentrations. Probit regression analysis provided effective LC 50 and LC 90 values, confirming the strong larvicidal activity of both extracts. Their use can not only reduce dependency on hazardous synthetic insecticides but also support the development of greener strategies within integrated mosquito management programs.

title: Satellite-Derived Environmental Indices as Predictors of Arboviral Outbreak Risk in Sub-Saharan Africa: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis of Land Surface Temperature, NDVI, and Rainfall Estimates
abstract: This project contains the protocol, documentation, and supplementary materials for a systematic review and meta-analysis investigating the predictive value of satellite-derived environmental indices, including Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI), Land Surface Temperature (LST), and satellite-estimated rainfall, for arboviral outbreak risk across Sub-Saharan Africa. The review will synthesise evidence from primary studies evaluating the use of remote sensing and Earth observation data for predicting dengue, chikungunya, Rift Valley fever, yellow fever, West Nile virus, and other arboviral diseases. The protocol follows the PRISMA-P 2015 reporting guideline and includes predefined eligibility criteria, search strategies, risk of bias assessment methods, and plans for quantitative and narrative synthesis.

title: De veranderende epidemiologie van vectorziekten
abstract: Het augustusnummer van het Tijdschrift voor Geneeskunde en Gezondheidszorg bevat een bijdrage over virusinfecties met “exotische” muggen in de rol van vector (1). Intuïtief maken wij dan de associatie met verre reizen. Maar, er is meer aan de hand. “Vector-borne diseases” of vectorziekten vertegenwoordigen 17% van alle infectieziekten wereldwijd en zijn verantwoordelijk voor meer dan 700.000 overlijdens per jaar (2, 3). Die vectoren zijn artropoden (zoals muggen en teken) die pathogene micro-organismen (virussen, parasieten of bacteriën) kunnen overdragen op een gastheer wanneer zij een bloedmaaltijd gebruiken (2). Het gaat over koortsige ziekten zoals bijvoorbeeld malaria, gele koorts, dengue, chikungunya en zika. Het risico om zo een infectie op te lopen, is het grootst in die delen van de wereld met een warm en vochtig klimaat (3). Maar, in de voorbije 2 decennia was er een merkelijke toename in incidentie en verdeling van sommige van deze ziekten in Europa (4, 5). Dat heeft deels te maken met de toenemende globalisering, meer intercontinentaal reisverkeer en handelstranport wereldwijd, wat de verspreiding van vectoren in de hand werkt (4, 6). Terugkerende reizigers kunnen inderdaad een door vectoren overgebrachte infectie oplopen als “importziekte” omdat zij tijdens hun verblijf in een endemische streek gestoken werden door exotische muggen. Maar toch wordt ook in Europa in toenemende mate “autochtone transmissie” van door muggen overdraagbare pathogenen beschreven (7). De transmissie gebeurt dan doordat een teruggekeerde reiziger met viremie in eigen land geprikt wordt door een mug die een geschikte vector is, daarbij het pathogene micro-organisme opneemt en het dan doorgeeft aan een nog niet geïnfecteerd iemand bij een volgende prik (6). Een essentiële voorwaarde voor dit mechanisme is uiteraard dat de vector zich in het nieuwe land gevestigd heeft en zich daar kan handhaven. Meer en meer wordt aangenomen dat de klimaatverandering in belangrijke mate dit process aandrijft (8, 9). Hogere temperaturen, andere neerslagpatronen en zachtere winters zouden de vestiging en verspreiding van vectorartropoden in voordien niet-endemische regio’s mogelijk maken. Het gaat dan vooral om muggen van het species Aedes, Anopheles en Culex, en “sandflies” van het species Phlebotomus (8). Het ectothermische karakter van deze artropoden, die de eigen lichaamstemperatuur niet kunnen reguleren, maakt hen zeer gevoelig aan externe klimaatomstandigheden. Daarnaast is de omgevingstemperatuur mee bepalend voor de maturatie en replicatie van de pathogenen die door die atropoden meegedragen worden (10, 11). Op dezelfde manier wordt overigens ook de natuurlijke epidemiologie beïnvloed van ziekten die reeds autochtoon waren in Europa, zoals leishmaniasis, met sandflies als vector, en infectie met West Nile-virus, met Culex-muggen als vector (8). Aedes albopictus of de Aziatische tijgermug, vector van arbovirussen zoals dengue en chikungunya, is een voorbeeld bij uitstek van een exotische muggensoort die zich gestaag blijft verspreiden over het Europese continent na daar voor het eerst verschenen te zijn in de late jaren 70. Zo werd de eerste autochtone uitbraak van chikungunya in Europa gedocumenteerd in Italië in 2007, en van dengue in Kroatië in 2010. Later volgden herhaalde uitbraken van deze ziekten in Italië, Frankrijk en Spanje (6, 12). België ligt op het pad van de verder noordwaartse verplaatsing van deze mug, die zich er in toenemende mate vestigt en ook overwintert. Dat is gebleken uit projecten van surveillance, zoals MEMO en MEMO+ (acroniem voor “Monitoring of Exotic Mosquitoes”) als onderdeel van het groter “National Environmental Health Action Plan” of NEHAP (13, 14, 15). Observaties in andere delen van de wereld hebben aangetoond dat plaatselijke uitbraken van virusziekte overgebracht door Aedes-muggen zich typisch voordeden met een interval van 5 tot 15 jaar nadat deze muggensoort zich gevestigd had (5, 16). Europese data lijken de mogelijkheid van een dergelijk patroon te ondersteunen, want zij tonen een sterke toename van autochtone gevallen van dengue in landen waar Aedes albopictus al sinds meerdere jaren gedijt (5). Deze bevindingen moeten ons er dus toe aanzetten om de kans op een ernstige infectieziekte overgebracht door muggen niet meer louter als een “ver-van-mijn-bedhypothese” weg te dringen wanneer in de anamnese een typische hint zoals “terugkeer van een verre reis” ontbreekt. Want hoewel nu misschien nog geen vaste prik in onze standaardlijst van differentiaaldiagnosen van een koortsige ziekte, kan de optie van een door muggen overdraagbare infectie in de toekomst mogelijk vaker het overwegen waard worden. Patrick Lacor, hoofdredacteur

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study addresses the changing epidemiology of vector-borne diseases, focusing on the emergence of exotic mosquito-borne infections in Europe and the role of climate change in their spread.
analysis.study_design_and_population: This is a narrative review discussing global and European epidemiological trends, surveillance projects, and case studies of autochthonous outbreaks without a specific study population or experimental design.
analysis.methods: The analysis is based on literature review and surveillance data from projects like MEMO and MEMO+, examining the establishment and spread of exotic mosquito species and associated diseases in Europe.
analysis.main_results: Vector-borne diseases represent 17% of all infectious diseases globally, with over 700,000 deaths annually; autochthonous transmission of diseases like chikungunya and dengue has been documented in Europe since 2007, with increasing incidence in regions where Aedes albopictus is established.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The authors interpret climate change as a key driver for the establishment and spread of exotic vectors in Europe, challenging the perception of mosquito-borne infections as solely 'imported' diseases and highlighting the need for updated diagnostic approaches.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings emphasize the need to include mosquito-borne infections in differential diagnoses for febrile illnesses, even without a history of travel, and to strengthen surveillance and preparedness for emerging vector-borne diseases in Europe.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The evidence is based on observational data and literature review, with moderate strength due to the lack of primary experimental data but supported by multiple surveillance projects and documented outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This review examines the changing epidemiology of vector-borne diseases in Europe, focusing on the role of exotic mosquitoes like Aedes albopictus in spreading infections such as chikungunya and dengue. The authors highlight that while global travel initially introduced these diseases, climate change now facilitates autochthonous transmission in Europe. Surveillance data shows increasing outbreaks in countries where exotic vectors have established, challenging the assumption that mosquito-borne infections are solely imported. The study underscores the need for clinicians to consider local transmission in differential diagnoses and for public health systems to adapt to this emerging threat through enhanced surveillance and preparedness.

Het gaat over koortsige ziekten zoals bijvoorbeeld malaria, gele koorts, dengue, chikungunya en zika. Het risico om zo een infectie op te lopen, is het grootst in die delen van de wereld met een warm en vochtig klimaat (3). Maar, in de voorbije 2 decennia was er een merkelijke toename in incidentie en verdeling van sommige van deze ziekten in Europa (4, 5). Dat heeft deels te maken met de toenemende globalisering, meer intercontinentaal reisverkeer en handelstranport wereldwijd, wat de verspreiding van vectoren in de hand werkt (4, 6). Terugkerende reizigers kunnen inderdaad een door vectoren overgebrachte infectie oplopen als “importziekte” omdat zij tijdens hun verblijf in een endemische streek gestoken werden door exotische muggen. Maar toch wordt ook in Europa in toenemende mate “autochtone transmissie” van door muggen overdraagbare pathogenen beschreven (7). De transmissie gebeurt dan doordat een teruggekeerde reiziger met viremie in eigen land geprikt wordt door een mug die een geschikte vector is, daarbij het pathogene micro-organisme opneemt en het dan doorgeeft aan een nog niet geïnfecteerd iemand bij een volgende prik (6). Een essentiële voorwaarde voor dit mechanisme is uiteraard dat de vector zich in het nieuwe land gevestigd heeft en zich daar kan handhaven. Meer en meer wordt aangenomen dat de klimaatverandering in belangrijke mate dit process aandrijft (8, 9). Hogere temperaturen, andere neerslagpatronen en zachtere winters zouden de vestiging en verspreiding van vectorartropoden in voordien niet-endemische regio’s mogelijk maken. Het gaat dan vooral om muggen van het species Aedes, Anopheles en Culex, en “sandflies” van het species Phlebotomus (8). Het ectothermische karakter van deze artropoden, die de eigen lichaamstemperatuur niet kunnen reguleren, maakt hen zeer gevoelig aan externe klimaatomstandigheden. Daarnaast is de omgevingstemperatuur mee bepalend voor de maturatie en replicatie van de pathogenen die door die atropoden meegedragen worden (10, 11). Op dezelfde manier wordt overigens ook de natuurlijke epidemiologie beïnvloed van ziekten die reeds autochtoon waren in Europa, zoals leishmaniasis, met sandflies als vector, en infectie met West Nile-virus, met Culex-muggen als vector (8). Aedes albopictus of de Aziatische tijgermug, vector van arbovirussen zoals dengue en chikungunya, is een voorbeeld bij uitstek van een exotische muggensoort die zich gestaag blijft verspreiden over het Europese continent na daar voor het eerst verschenen te zijn in de late jaren 70. Zo werd de eerste autochtone uitbraak van chikungunya in Europa gedocumenteerd in Italië in 2007, en van dengue in Kroatië in 2010. Later volgden herhaalde uitbraken van deze ziekten in Italië, Frankrijk en Spanje (6, 12). België ligt op het pad van de verder noordwaartse verplaatsing van deze mug, die zich er in toenemende mate vestigt en ook overwintert. Dat is gebleken uit projecten van surveillance, zoals MEMO en MEMO+ (acroniem voor “Monitoring of Exotic Mosquitoes”) als onderdeel van het groter “National Environmental Health Action Plan” of NEHAP (13, 14, 15). Observaties in andere delen van de wereld hebben aangetoond dat plaatselijke uitbraken van virusziekte overgebracht door Aedes-muggen zich typisch voordeden met een interval van 5 tot 15 jaar nadat deze muggensoort zich gevestigd had (5, 16). Europese data lijken de mogelijkheid van een dergelijk patroon te ondersteunen, want zij tonen een sterke toename van autochtone gevallen van dengue in landen waar Aedes albopictus al sinds meerdere jaren gedijt (5). Deze bevindingen moeten ons er dus toe aanzetten om de kans op een ernstige infectieziekte overgebracht door muggen niet meer louter als een “ver-van-mijn-bedhypothese” weg te dringen wanneer in de anamnese een typische hint zoals “terugkeer van een verre reis” ontbreekt. Want hoewel nu misschien nog geen vaste prik in onze standaardlijst van differentiaaldiagnosen van een koortsige ziekte, kan de optie van een door muggen overdraagbare infectie in de toekomst mogelijk vaker het overwegen waard worden. Patrick Lacor, hoofdredacteur

analysis_zh.research_question_and_background: 该研究探讨了 媒介 传播疾病的变化,重点关注欧洲外来蚊媒感染的出现以及气候变化在其传播中的作用。
analysis_zh.study_design_and_population: 这是一篇叙述性评论,讨论全球和欧洲流行病学趋势、监测 项目以及本土 暴发 的案例研究,没有特定的研究人群或实验设计。
analysis_zh.methods: 该分析基于文献综述和来自 MEMO 和 MEMO+ 等项目的 监测 数据,研究了欧洲外来蚊子物种和相关疾病的建立和传播。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 作者将气候变化解释为外来 媒介 在欧洲建立和传播的关键驱动因素,挑战了蚊媒感染仅作为“输入”疾病的看法,并强调了更新诊断方法的必要性。

title: The prediction of Aedes mosquito abundance using remote sensing and machine learning in Harris County, Texas
abstract: Vector-borne diseases, particularly those transmitted by Aedes mosquitoes, remain a major public health challenge globally, with species like Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus as primary vectors of dengue, chikungunya, and Zika viruses. The management of these mosquitoes is complicated by their adaptability to urban environments and the resource limitations of mosquito control programs. This study presents a proof-of-concept approach to improve Aedes surveillance and control by integrating remote sensing data and machine learning techniques. We used Sentinel-2 satellite imagery and environmental data to predict Aedes abundance across Harris County, Texas, incorporating both weather and socioeconomic features into predictive models. Using XGBoost, a machine learning algorithm, we identified high-risk areas for mosquito abundance with increased accuracy over traditional methods. This study demonstrates the potential of combining remote sensing with machine learning for enhancing mosquito surveillance programs, offering an innovative new strategy to improve vector control and mitigate the spread of mosquito-borne diseases. Future research should explore broader geographic applications and additional environmental variables to further refine predictive models.

full_text: Abstract Background Acute febrile illnesses are common causes of seeking health care in Sub-Sahara Africa especially among the under-five years. Understanding their causative pathogen is critical for optimal patient management. We characterized a febrile illness outbreak in Marsabit County to determine the magnitude of an outbreak, describe the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of the outbreak and conduct Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE). Methods A retrospective review of laboratory registers and patients’ clinical notes was done at Kargi Health Centre, Korr Health Centre and Laisamis Sub-county Hospital. A case of febrile illness was any person living in or has travelled to Laisamis Sub-county presenting with fever ≥ 380 C or headache at the health facility or in the community from 1st May to 24th May 2023. Cases of febrile illness were interviewed using a structured questionnaire to collect clinical and epidemiologic information. Approximately 4–5 ml of blood was collected from cases of febrile illness for laboratory differential diagnosis. Risk Communication and Community Engagement activities were conducted included interpersonal communication, focused manyatta group discussions and sensitization of community health promoters. Results A total of 184 febrile cases were line listed. Eighteen cases of Chikungunya and 12 cases of malaria were confirmed from the 72-blood specimen analysed during the investigation period. Understanding their causative pathogen is critical for optimal patient management. We characterized a febrile illness outbreak in Marsabit County to determine the magnitude of an outbreak, describe the epidemiology and clinical characteristics of the outbreak and conduct Risk Communication and Community Engagement (RCCE). Methods A retrospective review of laboratory registers and patients’ clinical notes was done at Kargi Health Centre, Korr Health Centre and Laisamis Sub-county Hospital. A case of febrile illness was any person living in or has travelled to Laisamis Sub-county presenting with fever ≥ 380 C or headache at the health facility or in the community from 1st May to 24th May 2023. Cases of febrile illness were interviewed using a structured questionnaire to collect clinical and epidemiologic information. Approximately 4–5 ml of blood was collected from cases of febrile illness for laboratory differential diagnosis. Risk Communication and Community Engagement activities were conducted included interpersonal communication, focused manyatta group discussions and sensitization of community health promoters. Results A total of 184 febrile cases were line listed. Eighteen cases of Chikungunya and 12 cases of malaria were confirmed from the 72-blood specimen analysed during the investigation period. Of the 12 samples that tested positives for malaria, 11 were P. falciparum and one P. vivax. Of the 72 blood specimen analysed, three had dual infection. One mortality was reported, involving a case co-infected with Malaria P. falciparum and Chikungunya. Thirteen Manyattas were visited where interpersonal communication was conducted as well as focused group discussion among manyatta residents and manyatta leaders. Two hundred Community Health Volunteers were sensitized on mosquito-borne diseases prevention and control in Laisamis Town. There was low knowledge on causes of febrile illness especially malaria. Conclusions The outbreak was driven by two infections; Chikungunya virus infection and Malaria infection. Sustained surveillance, vector control programs and awareness promotion are needed for early detection and control of possible mosquito-borne outbreaks. title_original: Malaria and Chikungunya outbreak in Marsabit County, Kenya, May 2023: a descriptive study

analysis.research_question_and_background: Understanding the causative pathogen of acute febrile illnesses is critical for optimal patient management in Sub-Saharan Africa, especially among the under-five years.
analysis.study_design_and_population: A retrospective review of laboratory registers and patients' clinical notes was conducted at Kargi Health Centre, Korr Health Centre and Laisamis Sub-county Hospital from 1st May to 24th May 2023.
analysis.methods: Cases of febrile illness were interviewed using a structured questionnaire, and approximately 4–5 ml of blood was collected for laboratory differential diagnosis.
analysis.main_results: A total of 184 febrile cases were line-listed, with 18 cases of Chikungunya and 12 cases of malaria confirmed from 72 blood specimens analyzed; 11 malaria cases were P. falciparum and one was P. vivax, with three dual infections reported.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The study identified a co-infection of Malaria P. falciparum and Chikungunya in one fatal case, highlighting the need for differential diagnosis in febrile illness outbreaks.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: Findings emphasize the importance of surveillance for both malaria and Chikungunya in outbreak-prone areas and the need for community sensitization on mosquito-borne disease prevention.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study was retrospective and limited to three health facilities, with low community knowledge on febrile illness causes, suggesting moderate evidence strength due to potential selection bias.

analysis.summary_en: This descriptive study investigated a febrile illness outbreak in Marsabit County, Kenya, in May 2023. A retrospective review of laboratory registers and clinical notes identified 184 cases, with 18 confirmed Chikungunya and 12 malaria cases (11 P. falciparum, one P. vivax) from 72 blood specimens. Three dual infections were reported, and one fatal case involved co-infection with Malaria P. falciparum and Chikungunya. Risk Communication and Community Engagement activities were conducted, including interpersonal communication and sensitization of 200 Community Health Volunteers. The study highlights the need for differential diagnosis and community education on mosquito-borne diseases in outbreak-prone areas.

elements_zh.research_question_and_background: 了解急性发热性疾病的致病病原体对于撒哈拉以南非洲地区(尤其是五岁以下儿童)的最佳患者管理至关重要。
elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 2023 年 5 月 1 日至 24 日,对 Kargi 健康中心、Korr 健康中心和 Laisamis 县医院的实验室登记册和患者临床记录进行了回顾性审查。
elements_zh.methods: 使用结构化问卷对发热性疾病病例进行访谈,并采集约 4-5 毫升血液用于实验室鉴别 诊断。
elements_zh.main_results: 共有184例发热病例被列入名单,其中18例基孔肯雅热病例和12例疟疾病例通过分析的72份血液样本得到证实;11 例疟疾病例为恶性疟原虫,1 例为间日疟原虫,报告了 3 例双重感染。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究在一例死亡病例中发现了恶性疟原虫和基孔肯雅热的双重感染,强调了在发热性疾病 暴发 中使用鉴别 诊断 的必要性。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了 暴发 对 暴发 多发地区的疟疾和基孔肯雅热的重要性,以及提高社区对蚊媒疾病预防认识的必要性。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性的,仅限于三个卫生机构,社区对发热性疾病原因的了解很少,表明由于潜在的选择偏差,证据强度中等。

analysis_zh.main_results: 共有184例发热病例被列入名单,其中18例基孔肯雅热病例和12例疟疾病例通过分析的72份血液样本得到证实;11 例疟疾病例为恶性疟原虫,1 例为间日疟原虫,报告了 3 例双重感染。
analysis_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 该研究在一例死亡病例中发现了恶性疟原虫和基孔肯雅热的双重感染,强调了在发热性疾病 暴发 中使用鉴别 诊断 的必要性。
analysis_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 研究结果强调了 暴发 对 暴发 多发地区的疟疾和基孔肯雅热的重要性,以及提高社区对蚊媒疾病预防认识的必要性。
analysis_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究是回顾性的,仅限于三个卫生机构,社区对发热性疾病原因的了解很少,表明由于潜在的选择偏差,证据强度中等。

full_text: Küba Seyahati Sonrası Gelişen İmporte Chikungunya Enfeksiyonu: Subakut Dönemde Persistan Enflamatuvar Artralji ile Seyreden Bir Olgu Imported Chikungunya Infection Following Travel to Cuba: A Case with Persistent Inflammatory Arthralgia in the Subacute Phase Meliha Çağla SÖNMEZER1(ID), Eylül Beren TANIK2(ID), Revasiye GÜLEŞEN2(ID), Şule APRAŞ BİLGEN3(ID), Murat AKOVA1(ID) 1 Hacettepe Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi, Enfeksiyon Hastalıkları ve Klinik Mikrobiyoloji Anabilim Dalı, Ankara. 1 Hacettepe University Faculty of Medicine, Department of Infectious Diseases and Clinical Microbiology, Ankara, Türkiye. 2 Türkiye Halk Sağlığı Kurumu, Mikrobiyoloji Referans Laboratuvarları Dairesi, Ankara. 2 Public Health Agency of Türkiye, Department of Microbiology Reference Laboratories, Ankara, Türkiye. 3 Hacettepe Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi, İç Hastalıkları Anabilim Dalı, Romatoloji Bilim Dalı, Ankara. 3 Hacettepe University Faculty of Medicine, Department of Internal Medicine, Division of Rheumatology, Ankara, Türkiye. ÖZ Alphavirus chikungunya, Aedes türü sivrisinekler aracılığıyla bulaşan ve genellikle ani başlangıçlı ateşle şiddetli poliartraljiye yol açan bir arbovirüstür. Enfeksiyon, akut dönemi takiben bazı hastalarda haftalar ya da aylar sürebilen persistan eklem yakınmalarıyla seyredebilmektedir. Artan uluslararası seyahatler ne­ deniyle, endemik olmayan ülkelerde importe chikungunya olgularının tanınması giderek daha önemli hale gelmiştir. Bu olguda, Küba seyahati sonrası ateş ve yaygın eklem ağrılarıyla başvuran 58 yaşında bir kadın hastada saptanan importe chikungunya enfeksiyonu sunulmuştur. Olgunun ilk değerlendirmesin­ de, C-reaktif protein düzeyleri belirgin yüksek bulunmuş, prokalsitonin düzeyleri normal sınırlarda sap­ tanmıştır. Ardışık serum örneklerinde chikungunya virüsüne özgü IgM pozitifliği ve IgG serokonversiyonu gösterilerek tanı doğrulanmıştır. Moleküler testlerde viral RNA saptanmamıştır. Dengue, Zika ve diğer arbovirüs enfeksiyonları ile romatolojik hastalıklar ayırıcı tanıda dışlanmıştır. Hasta antipiretikler ve nons­ teroid antienflamatuvar ilaçlar ile tedavi edilmiş ancak eklem ağrılarının persistan olması ve günlük yaşam aktivitelerini ciddi biçimde kısıtlaması nedeniyle opioid analjeziklere geçilmiştir. Subakut (post-akut) chi­ kungunya ilişkili enflamatuvar artralji ön tanısıyla sistemik kortikosteroid tedavisi denenmiş ve kısmi klinik yanıt alınmıştır. Semptom süresinin üç aydan kısa olması nedeniyle kronik chikungunya artriti düşünül­ memiş ve hastalık modifiye edici antiromatizmal ilaç başlanmamıştır. Bu olgu, endemik olmayan ülkelerde seyahat öyküsü olan hastalarda chikungunya enfeksiyonunun, döküntü bulunmasa dahi, ateş ve persistan artralji varlığında mutlaka ayırıcı tanıda düşünülmesi gerektiğini vurgulamaktadır. Subakut dönemde uy­ gun semptomatik tedavi ve yakın izlem, kronikleşmenin önlenmesi açısından önem taşımaktadır. Anahtar kelimeler: Chikungunya; arbovirüs; importe enfeksiyon; subakut dönem; enflamatuvar artralji; seyahat ilişkili enfeksiyon. Olgu Sunumu/Case Report İletişim (Correspondence): Doç. Dr.Meliha Çağla Sönmezer, Hacettepe Üniversitesi Tıp Fakültesi, Enfeksiyon Hastalıkları ve Klinik Mikrobiyoloji Anabilim Dalı, Ankara, Türkiye.
